title: Nobody has ever judged whether 44% any-answer is enough; the listing and paywall promise a verdict on every cart item, and 1 scan in 6 to 4 delivers one
evidence: Promise: docs/store/listing.md promo text 'Scan a barcode, enter the shelf price, and know in seconds if it's a great, good, reasonable or bad price. Check every price in your cart before you pay.'; description 'Is this a good price? Pexi tells you in seconds, right at the shelf.'; PEXI PLUS 'Pexi Plus gives you 100 barcode scans a week, enough to check your whole cart'. Paywall (app/public/js/ui-strings.js:71,73,106): 'Check every price in your cart', '100 barcode scans every week, enough to check your whole cart.' Delivery: REPORT.md line 20 (Mac scan table, 14 days, 19 phones, 109 scans, read once by round 1): 44% any answer, 17.4% a shop price and verdict. NOW.md:69 (older, 176 scans, Nov 14/15): 27% had a shop price. Brief says about a quarter. Three different figures for the shop-price share on different dates and definitions; the Mac breakdown job should settle it. Popular-barcode probe (functions.jsonl, answers.csv, 191 Open Food Facts barcodes, no Claude consent): 98 priced (51%), explicitly optimistic because it uses the catalogue's own source. Business case (grep of docs for answer rate, hit rate, coverage; docs/decisions.md 2026-11-05 pricing ruling; round2/cost-table.md): no document sets a target answer rate; the pricing ruling assumes 1 in 100 users pay and a 60% repeat-cache share (estimate, unmeasured), docs/the-moonshot.md:122 says 'Answer rate 100% by design' (a different design); premortem round 2 recommended a launch gate 'for example half' on the shop-price share and nothing in the register adopts it (grep REGISTER.md: R24 only says nobody reads the weekly numbers).
fix: Jamin sets one number before submission: the share of real scans that get a shop price and verdict that he would accept (round 2 suggested half), and the date it is read. Until it is met, the first screenshots, subtitle and paywall already lead with a verdict; keep them, but fill the most-scanned unpriced barcodes first and read the figure weekly (scripts/funnel-report.mjs exists).
fix_cost: decision 10 minutes, $0; the data fill is the real cost (days of crawler work)
dup_of: adds to premortem round 2 'Most scans come back without a real shop price' and R24; new: the three conflicting figures, and that no document states a target answer rate

title: A first-time shopper's first three scans: about a 4 in 5 chance of at least one answer of any kind, only about a 2 in 5 to 3 in 5 chance of one real shop-price verdict
evidence: Arithmetic, assuming each scan is independent and a new shopper behaves like the 19 testers (neither is checked; the testers were friends and testers, scanning what they chose; a first-time shopper in the aisle scans ordinary groceries, which the 51% popular-barcode probe suggests may be easier, but that probe is optimistic by its own caveat). With p(any answer)=0.44: 1-0.56^3 = 82% at least one answer, 18% none of three. With p(shop price and verdict)=0.174 (REPORT.md): 1-0.826^3 = 44% at least one priced verdict, expected 0.52 priced scans of 3, all three priced 0.5%. With p=0.25 (brief) or 0.27 (NOW.md): 58% to 61%, expected 0.75 to 0.81 of 3. With p=0.51 (popular-barcode probe, upper bound): 88%. The first scan alone is a priced verdict 17% to 27% of the time. Not measured: scans per first session or whether the same phone's first three scans differ from the average (the Mac breakdown job is pulling the live detail).
fix: Ask the Mac job for per-device first-three-scans outcomes from the scan log (real, not modelled) and replace this estimate. For the shopper in the meantime: the answer on a miss must name the next step in one line (type the name, enter the shelf price); round 1 business rank 10 covers the wording.
fix_cost: one read-only query on the Mac, minutes
dup_of: none (the estimate is new; business rank 6 used 10 x 0.27 for the free tier only)

title: The 10 free scans are spent on answers that are not the product: a free shopper gets about 2 to 3 priced verdicts before the wall, and Plus's 100 scans buy about 17 to 27 priced verdicts a week
evidence: app/src/scan-quota.ts header (read today, unchanged by the latest commit a156678 as far as the header goes): a scan counts when kind='barcode', outcome='answered' and resolved_label is not null, 'Repeat scans served from the cache count: the shopper got an answer'. So a category-average or Claude-estimate answer with no shop price spends one of 10, while a total miss (no name) does not. Expected priced verdicts per 10 scans: 10 x 0.174 = 1.7 to 10 x 0.27 = 2.7 (same shares as above). Plus: 100 x 0.174 = 17 to 27 a week. The paywall (ui-strings.js:106) says the 100 is 'enough to check your whole cart'; what it buys is 100 attempts, of which about 1 in 6 to 1 in 4 return a shop-price verdict. Round 1 business rank 6 found the counting rule; what it did not do was tie it to what Plus buys.
fix: Count a scan against the limit only when its answer has shop prices (rank 6 fix), so Plus's 100 are 100 real verdicts; or leave the count and accept that the paywall sells attempts. Decide before the first paid sale, because refund requests after a first week of mostly broad ranges are the likely cost.
dup_of: business rank 6 and premortem 'free tier gives away the core product'; new: Plus-side arithmetic and the refund angle

title: Plus has one feature, a bigger weekly count, so the 3.1.2 'ongoing value' test rests entirely on the answer rate; a paid reviewer-or-user week with mostly broad estimates is weak ground
evidence: Apple, https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/ (fetched 2026-11-21), 3.1.2(a): 'If you offer an auto-renewable subscription, you must provide ongoing value to the customer'; examples listed include 'apps that offer consistent, substantive updates; access to large collections of, or continually updated, media content; software as a service'. Pexi's weekly price refresh (mac/hammer-refresh.sh per listing.md) is the closest fit, but the paywall sells only count: ui-strings.js:104,106 and you_plus_on 'Pexi Plus: 100 barcode scans a week'; the only difference between free and paid is the number. Round 1 apple-rules.jsonl treated 3.1.2 only for the renewal text and links (item 3 'unlimited scans' text, listing wording); it has no entry on ongoing value. I am not saying Apple would reject on this alone; I found no Apple text defining a threshold, so the probability is assumed. The practical exposure is a reviewer who buys in sandbox and sees the same answers as before.
fix: If Jamin wants a stronger answer to 3.1.2 and to buyers: give Plus something that grows with time (watch-list price-change notices are already a listed idea in round 2 premortem) or state the weekly price refresh on the paywall. A paywall line is a copy change, not a build.
fix_cost: a copy line 10 minutes; watch-list alerts are a multi-day build
dup_of: premortem round 2 'free tier gives away the core product' (conversion angle); new: the Apple 3.1.2(a) quote and that round 1 did not cover it

title: Apple 4.2 'adequate utility' and 4.3(b) are judgement calls where a reviewer's own three scans decide; the review notes steer them to a known-good barcode but also say the app 'answers every scan'
evidence: https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/ 4.2: 'If your app is not particularly useful, unique, or "app-like," it doesn't belong on the App Store. If your App doesn't provide some sort of lasting entertainment value or adequate utility, it may not be accepted.' 4.3(b): 'Don't submit apps that are indistinguishable from what's already widely available.' Round 1 apple-rules.jsonl covered 4.2 only as 'enough native value beyond a website' (native plugins list) and called it 'a judgement'; it did not cover utility or 4.3(b). New: (1) docs/store/listing.md App Review notes give the reviewer UPC 055773000795 and a typed example 'McCain Tasti Taters' so the first scan will be a good one, which protects review but means the reviewer never sees the 56% no-answer path; if the reviewer also scans something at hand outside Canada, the catalogue is Canadian (listing 'for shoppers in Canada') and the answer will be a miss. (2) The notes say 'the app answers every scan with both' (consent choices); read alone it can be taken as 'answers every scan', which round 1 business and REPORT show is not true (44%). Apple 2.3.1(a) (same page): 'marketing your app in a misleading way, such as by promoting content or services that it does not actually offer'. The notes say 'If it ever shows no answer, please retry in a few minutes', which blames the connection, not coverage. (3) 4.3(b): competitors are free and widely installed (see next finding), but none gives a verdict on the shelf price in your hand (business competitors row), which is the argument for 'meaningfully different'.
fix: Reword the review note to say Pexi covers common Canadian groceries and shows 'Pexi doesn't know this one yet' for others, with the known barcode as the demo; say in one line what makes Pexi different from a flyer app (a verdict on the price in hand).
dup_of: apple-rules round 1 item on 4.2 (adds utility and 4.3(b) angle and the 'answers every scan' wording)

title: Subtitle 'Know if it's a deal' is a claim Apple 2.3.7 tells developers not to make if unverifiable, and the shopper's alternatives are free
evidence: https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/ 2.3.7: 'App subtitles ... should not include inappropriate content, reference other apps, or make unverifiable product claims.' docs/store/listing.md subtitle: 'Scan it. Know if it's a deal.' Pexi's own TEMPLATES.md:137 says 'NOT MEASURED: how often the price range or the tier matches what a shop actually charges next week. No hit rate exists' and legal-review-2026-11-17.md:203 asks for a measured hit-rate note (gap 60, still open). Round 1 apple-rules.jsonl has no 2.3.7 entry (grep count 0). 'Deal' also edges toward a savings promise (hard rule 2: no savings claim until measured), though the line does not state an amount.
fix: Use a subtitle that describes the action and not the result, for example 'Scan it. See the price range.' (28 of 30), or keep the current one and accept a metadata rejection risk that I rate low; Jamin's call.
dup_of: gap 60 (hit rate note) and business rank 2 (store text); new: 2.3.7 quote

title: What a Canadian shopper already has for 'is this a good price' is free and bigger; Pexi must win on the in-hand verdict, and at 17% to 27% priced it often cannot
evidence: Apple lookup API, country=ca, fetched 2026-11-21 (api https://itunes.apple.com/lookup?id=<id>&country=ca; store pages in parentheses). Flipp (https://apps.apple.com/ca/app/flipp-flyers-shopping-deals/id725097967): price 'Free', 4.72 from 865,264 ratings; description 'Flipp is your ultimate grocery savings and price matching tool ... Plan ahead with flyers, coupons, and your shopping list, all in one place! Easily save money on grocery shopping and compare food prices from: Walmart Canada, Real Canadian Superstore, Save on Foods, Freshco, Safeway, Food Basics, Giant Tiger, Fortinos'. (Flipp's own savings figure in that text is not repeated here, hard rule 2.) PC Optimum (https://apps.apple.com/ca/app/pc-optimum/id634040057): Free, 3.12 from 36,673 ratings; 'The rewards program unlike any other. With exclusive events and offers based on the items you buy most ... Load offers, earn and redeem points and manage your account'; a store loyalty app, not a price check. Canadian Grocery Flyers & Deal (https://apps.apple.com/ca/app/canadian-grocery-flyers-deal/id6753903055): Free to download, 3.91 from 22 ratings; 'Get instant price drop alerts, compare deals across stores, browse weekly flyers'; 'See prices for the same product across all stores near you'; business job quoted its subscription as $3.99 monthly, $7.99 yearly. Price Scanner Barcode (https://apps.apple.com/ca/app/price-scanner-barcode/id728175625): 'Free · In-App Purchases', 4.4 from 517 ratings, 'Scan UPC Barcodes for FREE and Save Money. Amazon, Best Buy, Target, Walmart, etc.' and 'quickly find the BEST price', ad-free purchases $2.99, $3.99, $17.99; US retailers named. Google Lens (https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/shopping/visual-search-lens-shopping/): 'instantly see details like price across retailers, current deals, product reviews and where to buy it', rolling out 'for Android and iOS devices in select countries'; the page does not say whether Canada is one, nor name a price; free to use inside the Google app (assumed, not stated on the page). Competitors' quoted claims were not tested against reality. Business round 1 (rank 'Competitors') already had Flipp, Yuka and three scanners; new here: PC Optimum, Google Lens and the 'what each gives' comparison.
fix: Position as the check for the price in your hand that none of the above gives (business round 1 recommendation), and do not charge anyone a monthly fee while the free tools answer store-by-store flyer prices at 865K-rating scale. A Plus price of CA$3.99 a month equals Canadian Grocery Flyers' monthly price, which has 22 ratings.
dup_of: business round 1 'Competitors' row (adds PC Optimum, Google Lens, per-app description quotes)

title: The business case has no answer-rate assumption at all, only a 1-in-100 paying share and a cache share, so no number says what coverage makes Plus pay for itself
evidence: grep -rniE 'answer rate|hit rate|coverage rate|answered share|share of scans' across docs/*.md (excluding this review): the pricing ruling in docs/decisions.md (2026-11-05, 'we should assume only 1 in 100 people pay') derives US$1.55 a month per yearly payer, 1.55 US cents a month per user at 1 in 100, and assumes 'The repeat cache is assumed to answer 60 percent of scans (an estimate ... unmeasured)'; that is cost, not value. The falsifier it names, 'under 1 in 10 testers who reach the limit tap Subscribe', was never measured (round 2 premortem). docs/readiness/HANDOVER.md:66 says to log 'share of scans that showed a shop price' weekly but sets no threshold. At 17.4% to 27% priced scans, the only retained-value argument is the free half (typed search is free, uncounted), which is also why almost nobody needs Plus (premortem).
fix: Add one line to docs/decisions.md and the weekly log: target priced share, target paywall-to-subscribe, and the date each is read; decide continue or stop. Round 2 already asked for the second; the first is new.
dup_of: gap 89 (paywall number) and premortem 'Launched with no proof anyone will pay'; new: no coverage target exists
